changes_from_2026_08: 264 capacity values corrected to the published chart. The 2026-08 extract carried values that were consistently off by 5-25 lbs, none of which appear anywhere in the source document.

42 rows REMOVED: 40E and 40ER under an F3M (6", 3-tab) end plate. Page 84 publishes F3M for 27E and 36E only, and page 88 groups the 40E column under F4M. Character 13 of those rows' own codes reads 'C' (F3M) on a 40E beam, which the code format does not allow. They were a phantom variant: not published, and reading 3.8-12.2% BELOW the real 40E capacity, so the engine would have quoted a beam that does not exist while appearing conservative.

No part number, code_18 or deflection value was altered, and no capacity value was invented: 264 capacities were re-sourced to the published chart and 42 unpublished rows were removed. FACE HEIGHT WAS CORRECTED on 168 of the 336 rows - 36E/36ER 3.65 -> 3.65625 (3 21/32), 59E/59ER 5.92 -> 5.9375 (5 15/16), and 65E/65ER/65Q/65QR 6.54 -> 6.5625 (6 9/16) - to the exact fractions printed on p.84. The other eight families were already exact and did not move. See face_height_59e_status, face_height_65_status and face_height_policy for the reasoning and the approver. This sentence previously read 'no face height value was altered', which was false; corrected 2026-09-01 under review finding F-12. A change log that under-reports is the same defect as an extract that over-reports.

frames.json carried forward from 2026-08 UNCHANGED, so the approved release resolves a frame as well as a beam. Previously the three frame tables existed only in the DRAFT 2026-08 release, which canPinForNewRevision correctly refuses - so MVP checks 1 and 2 could not resolve a frame from any pinnable revision. No frame value was altered; the tables SHA-256 is recorded in frames.json and asserted by test.
code_basis: RMI guidelines and ANSI MH16.1-2012 (p.88 footnote); FY = 55 KSI

content_sha256_method.note: sha256 of json.dumps(beams.json['rows'], sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) encoded UTF-8 - the canonical rows array, not the file text. Written by tools/build-2026-09-manifest.py and tools/set-exact-face-heights.py. CAVEAT, recorded under review finding F-19: this digest depends on Python's float formatting. beams.json carries "face_height_in": 4.0 for the whole-number families; Python writes 4.0 and every other JSON implementation writes 4, so the same data yields a different digest anywhere but Python unless the original numeric literal is preserved. tools/check-content-hash.mjs preserves it and verifies this hash on every run. Re-basing the digest onto an implementation-independent form would change an APPROVED release, so it is left for the approver to decide rather than done here.

deflection_limit: L/180 (p.88: 'lesser of strength in bending, or L/180 deflection criteria')
disregarded: Mecalux Material Catalog (Mecalux_Material_Catalog.xlsx) - DISREGARDED FOR CAPACITY VALUES. It describes a different product line (25E, 31E, 35E, 39E, 43E, 47E, 55E, 65Q-DX) and carries no capacity data for twelve of the sixteen families this catalog covers (27E/27ER, 36E/36ER, 40E/40ER, 45E/45ER, 50ER, 59ER, 65ER, 65QR). Where both sources do overlap they disagree on every span - e.g. 65E at 48" reads 17,115 lbs in PSG 2025 and 15,000 lbs in the Material Catalog. A prior reconciliation recommended using the Material Catalog for capacity lookups; that recommendation is superseded as IMPOSSIBLE TO SATISFY, not merely rejected - the data it points to does not exist for most of our families. Recorded here so a future reader does not 'restore' it under the impression it was dropped by accident.

face_height_59e_status.reason: P0-005 closed. Four figures had been in circulation - 5.92 (the 2026-08 transcription), 5.928 (a documentation table), 5.93 (the guide's own two-decimal rendering) and 5.9375 (the exact fraction). They were all approximations of one published value: p.84 prints 5 15/16". Storing the exact fraction ends the dispute rather than settling it, because there is no longer a rounding choice to disagree about. 5.92 appears nowhere in the source document.

face_height_65_status.reason: The 2026-08 extract carried 6.54 for 65E/65ER/65Q/65QR, which matches neither the printed fraction 6 9/16 (6.5625) nor the guide's own two-decimal rendering (6.56). Found by the page-84 cross-check that resolved 59E, and closed by the same policy decision: store the exact fraction.

face_height_policy.reason: Face height enters an elevation stack once per beam level, and rounding or truncating errs the same direction every time, so the error accumulates rather than cancelling: a one-decimal STORED value drifts up to about 1.25" over a 20-level stack (65E), which exceeds the ~1/4" a pallet opening is specified to, and it drifts in the direction that reports MORE clear height than exists. The engine therefore stores the exact published fraction and the interface rounds for display only. 27E and 45E are printed as exact values (2 3/4, 4 1/2), so a one-decimal store would have discarded a digit the manufacturer actually published.

load_basis: Uniformly distributed product load plus dead load, PER PAIR of beams (dead load = weight of beams). Static load only. Value is the lesser of strength in bending and L/180 deflection.
approval_record: APPROVED 2026-09-01 by Elliott Villacorta, after one return to DRAFT on the same day. The first approval was made against a 20-cell beam sample that covered only 19 distinct PUBLISHED values: p.88 prints one column per E/ER pair, and the draw landed on both halves of one printed cell. The 42 recorded cells were the drawn cells and every one matched - the gate was measuring the wrong thing, not accepting a fabricated record. The release was returned to DRAFT, the gate was changed to count distinct published values rather than extract rows, the pinned draw gained a deterministic one-cell top-up (65ER/F5M/78in), that cell was read off PSG 2025 p.88 and recorded MATCHED, and the release was re-approved. See human_spot_checks for the completed record. This field previously described the DRAFT state as current; corrected 2026-09-01 under review finding F-13.

verification_paths.note: All 336 capacity cells re-derived from PDF page 88 and compared against the shipped rows by packages/kernel-catalog/src/psg-authority.test.ts, which is wired into the test run. The chart was also parsed directly from the PDF independently of the supplied spreadsheet, and the two agree on every row. End-plate assignment cross-checked against page 84 and character 13 of each 18-digit code. COUNTING NOTE, recorded 2026-09-01 under review finding F-15: 'cells: 336' counts extract ROWS, and p.88 prints one column per E/ER pair - all eight pairs, all 21 spans, identical capacity - so the 336 rows carry 168 DISTINCT PUBLISHED VALUES. Each published value was therefore checked twice by construction. The cross-check is real; the number reports rows, not independent readings. The same asymmetry is why a 20-row random draw lands short of the section 10.2 floor of 20 READINGS by default, which is what the deterministic top-up exists for - the top-up is the normal case, not an exception. A future sampler should draw over distinct published values in the first place; changing the draw on an APPROVED release is the approver's call, so it is recorded here, not done.
